Today’s failing approach: in-house coding tests that your engineers build and mark
Failing approach 1
Engineer time
Your engineers write the test, keep it up to date and mark each submission by hand. Every new candidate adds marking time to an engineer’s week.
Failing approach 2
Leaked questions
If your in-house test reuses the same questions, a posted solution can give later candidates the answer before they start.
smart_toy
Failing approach 3
AI-generated answers
A candidate can paste a take-home task into an AI chat tool and submit the generated answer. The final answer alone does not show how the candidate produced the code.
extension_off
Failing approach 4
Tasks unlike the role
Your engineers can write an algorithm exercise faster than a realistic task.
HackerRank’s 2025 Developer Skills Report
found that 78% of developers say assessments don’t align with real-world tasks.
Replace your in-house coding test with validated work simulations
Codility Screen is a coding test platform for the screening stage of engineering hiring. Candidates complete realistic engineering tasks. You can include tasks built for a full VS Code environment. Your talent team then builds the shortlist for each role from the scored results.
Choose ready-made tasks instead of writing your own
You choose the tasks for each role from Codility’s library. The library covers technologies including React, Spring, Kubernetes and Terraform. Codility removes leaked tasks from the library.
Build with MCP also lets your engineers create tasks for parts of your stack that the library does not cover. An engineer describes the task to an AI coding assistant such as Claude, Cursor or GitHub Copilot.
The assistant then builds the task, its test cases and a reference solution. The engineer reviews the task before publishing it. Most tasks take about ten minutes from description to publication.
The difference:
Codility maintains the task library, so your engineers no longer keep the test up to date.

Score submissions automatically against test cases
Codility automatically scores the output of selected task types, including coding, bug-fixing, SQL and front-end tasks. Codility’s scoring is deterministic, so the same output always earns the same score.
You set the cut score, the minimum overall score that your team expects for the role. Your talent team then sees how many candidates reached the cut score. Codility connects with applicant tracking systems (ATS), including Greenhouse, Lever, Workday and SmartRecruiters. Codility stores each result in the candidate’s ATS record. Automatically scored tasks need no manual marking by your engineers.
Automatically scored tasks use the same scoring rules for every candidate.
Review how each candidate built the solution
Codility stores the submitted code and the test-case breakdown with each result, for the period set in your retention policy. Your engineers can open the Code Evolution Chart, a timeline of how the code changed during the assessment.
Codility can also collect integrity signals, which give reviewers evidence about how the candidate produced the submission. The signals include paste events, similarity checks against other candidates and identity verification.
You decide whether candidates can use the AI Assistant in each assessment. Where the AI Assistant is enabled, every candidate interaction is captured as reviewable AI activity.
Your reviewers see how the candidate reached the answer, in addition to the answer itself.

Questions about coding test platforms
A coding test platform gives candidates programming tasks and records their solutions. Codility Screen scores selected task types against test cases. An online coding test platform also stores the results for your hiring team. Talent teams use a coding test platform in place of tests that engineers write and mark by hand.
Replace them with realistic tasks on a platform that records how each candidate built the solution. Codility records a timeline of each candidate’s code changes. Codility also tests every task in its library for AI solvability. If your engineers use AI on the job, you can enable the AI Assistant. Reviewers then see every candidate interaction with the AI Assistant.
Buy a platform if your engineers spend their time writing, maintaining and marking tests. A platform supplies maintained tasks and scores selected task types automatically. Your engineers can review the results before deciding who advances. They can still create tasks for your own stack.
No. A person on your team decides who advances. Codility does not use AI or machine learning to make automated employment decisions.
